concerns.analysis: The source document contains organizational logos for 'The Security Awareness Company' at the bottom of pages 4 and 5. The HTML output contains comments indicating these images failed to render properly ('<!-- image without data: Logo for SAC the security awareness COMPANY -->'). As organizational logos are meaningful for identifying the author/agency of the content, their complete absence from the rendered output constitutes a failure.

concerns.description: Output has more images than source PDF (ratio 1.4x) — possible image duplication
concerns.analysis: image_count_ratio=1.40. More images in output than in source indicates duplicated or fabricated image elements.

concerns.description: Displaced hyperlinks: 14 link(s) extracted as standalone elements instead of inline text
concerns.analysis: standalone_links=14, examples=["Don't take the bait!", 'https://www.consumer.ftc.gov/articles/0074-giving-charity', 'https://www.cisecurity.org/resources/newsletter']. Links should be inline within paragraphs, not separate blocks.

concerns.description: Form elements detected: 1 form(s) with 8 field(s) — forms lose functionality in HTML
concerns.analysis: form_count=1, total_fields=8. PDF form fields (checkboxes, text inputs, signatures) cannot be faithfully rendered as static HTML.

The source document includes a sentence in the first paragraph that is completely underlined for emphasis ('You are the target, or to put it another way, the fish that bite.'). In the output JSON, the underline is lost entirely, and only the first part of the phrase was rendered with markdown italics.

concerns.output_quote: "*You are the target*, or to put it another way, the fish that bite."

concerns.description: Header/footer elements retained in output (4): 2; 3; © The Security Awareness Company, LLC
